user_input: Can I still get an ad-free Disney+ tier?
response: According to the current Terms of Service, Disney+ may now show ads on 'no ads'/'ad free' tiers, starting from January 27, 2025 for new subscribers and March 24, 2025 for existing ones. This means you may still be able to get an ad-free experience, but it could be subject to ad-insertion, depending on when you subscribed or re-subscribe. The Terms of Service do not specify when exactly ads will be shown, but it indicates that your ad-free experience might not be entirely ad-free starting from these dates.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DISNEY+ SUBSCRIBER AGREEMENT (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Disney+ and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective January 27, 2025 for new subscribers and March 24, 2025 for existing ones: streaming titles may now show ads even on 'no ads'/'ad free' tiers, expanded arbitration with mass-arbitration procedures following Disney's earlier 2024 Wrongful-Death-case controversy, and updated content-availability language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Disney+ to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.disneyplus.com/legal/subscriber-agreement . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.disneyplus.com/legal/subscriber-agreement .

[REFERENCE ANSWER]
Under the updated Subscriber Agreement (effective January 27, 2025 for new subscribers and March 24, 2025 for existing ones), the 'no ads' / 'ad-free' tiers may now include ads on certain streaming titles at Disney's discretion. So while the tier name remains, true ad-free playback is no longer guaranteed for all content.

- may include ads
- no ads
- no longer guaranteed

user_input: How do I keep my right to sue 23andMe after the data breach?
response: If you don't want to arbitrate any breach-related claims with 23andMe, you can opt out within 30 days after opening your account. Failure to opt out during this period will be considered a waiver of your right to pursue breach-related claims in court.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — 23ANDME TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2023; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with 23andMe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: After the October 2023 data breach, 23andMe updated its TOS to add a mandatory-arbitration clause and 30-day opt-out window, requiring users who didn't write to opt out to arbitrate any breach-related claims; also limited class-action rights and shortened the dispute-notice window.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by 23andMe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/full-version/2.0/ .
ground_truth:
[REFERENCE ANSWER]
Under the Terms updated after the October 2023 data breach, you are automatically opted in to mandatory arbitration unless you affirmatively opt out within the 30-day window described in the Terms by sending the company a written notice of objection. If you don't opt out, class-action rights are limited and disputes go to arbitration.
[MUST MENTION]
- mandatory arbitration
- 30-day
- opt out
- written

user_input: Is there a way to stop Tumblr from sharing my posts with AI partners?

Note that if you change this setting, your public posts will still be visible on Tumblr, but AI partners will not be able to use them for training purposes.

source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ADOBE GENERAL TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Adobe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: February 2024 update added language allowing Adobe to access user content via 'automated and manual methods' to improve services and software. After backlash in June 2024, Adobe rewrote sections in clearer language, explicitly stating it does not train generative-AI models on customer cloud content and added a plain-English summary of changes.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Adobe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.adobe.com/legal/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20231101000000*/https://www.adobe.com/legal/terms.html .

user_input: When was Google's Terms of Service last updated, and where can I see what changed?
response: According to the Terms of Service, the updated version took effect in 2024, replacing the 2022 version. If you're interested in seeing what changed between the two versions, a comparison page is provided by Google at `policies.google.com/terms/archive/20220105-20240522`.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — GOOGLE TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Google and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: Added language about generative AI features (e.g. content used to improve Google's AI services), clarified that abuse and reverse-engineering of AI models are prohibited, and updated the disputes/arbitration and liability sections. Comparison page provided by Google: policies.google.com/terms/archive/20220105-20240522.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Google to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://policies.google.com/terms?hl=en-US . The previous version is available at https://policies.google.com/terms/archive/20220105?hl=en-US .

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — YOUTUBE TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2021; replaces the 2019 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with YouTube and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2021 version differs from the 2019 version in the following ways: Effective June 1, 2021 globally: introduced YouTube's right to monetize most videos (including non-Partner videos), banned collection of facial-recognition data from videos, and updated US tax-withholding obligations for non-US creators. Summary at support.google.com/youtube/answer/10090902.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by YouTube to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.youtube.com/static?template=terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20191101000000*/https://www.youtube.com/static?template=terms .

user_input: How long do I have to wait before filing arbitration against Snap?
response:
If you have a dispute with Snap, most of the updated terms require binding arbitration with class-action waivers. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts, after which you will be subject to this dispute resolution method. This means, at a minimum, you will not be able to file suit in a court as an individual. 

However, if you do opt-out within 30 days of signing up for a new account, you can later choose to file a lawsuit in a court, rather than binding arbitration.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — SNAP TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Snap (Snapchat) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective April 7, 2025: added new sections on My AI and other generative-AI features, expanded the user-content license for Live/Local/crowd-sourced services, clarified data-sharing with parents (for under-18 users via Family Center), and updated arbitration pre-dispute notice procedures.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Snap (Snapchat) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.snap.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.snap.com/terms .

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Adobe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: February 2024 update added language allowing Adobe to access user content via 'automated and manual methods' to improve services and software. After backlash in June 2024, Adobe rewrote sections in clearer language, explicitly stating it does not train generative-AI models on customer cloud content and added a plain-English summary of changes.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Adobe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.

7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.adobe.com/legal/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20231101000000*/https://www.adobe.com/legal/terms.html .

user_input: Are the X 2024 Terms a meaningful change from the prior version?
response:
According to the terms, the 2024 version is a significant change from the prior version. Specifically, the Terms of Service mention three key changes:

* Added an explicit license for X (Twitter) to use posted content for training machine-learning and generative-AI models, effective November 15, 2024.
* Removed the prior in-product opt-out language.
* Broadened third-party data-sharing permissions.

These changes suggest that the 2024 Terms of Service update the way X uses user content, the options users have for opting out, and the sharing of user data with third parties.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — X TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with X (Twitter) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Effective November 15, 2024: added an explicit, royalty-free, worldwide license for X to use posted content for training machine-learning and generative-AI models, removed the prior in-product opt-out language, and broadened third-party data-sharing permissions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by X (Twitter) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://x.com/en/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240515000000*/https://twitter.com/en/tos .

[REFERENCE ANSWER]
Yes — the November 15, 2024 update is a substantive change. It explicitly extends X's worldwide, royalty-free license to cover training of machine-learning and generative-AI models, and the in-product opt-out language that had previously let users disable use of their content for Grok training was removed from the Terms. Third-party data-sharing permissions were also broadened. The bot should describe these changes without making sweeping claims about their legality.

- royalty-free

- removed

response: The Terms of Service say that Zoom "does not use audio, video or chat content to train AI models without customer consent." This is an amendment that was made in response to user feedback in August 2023. However, the Terms do describe how user-submitted content (like video calls) is used by Zoom to operate, improve and train its AI/ML systems, but it seems that Zoom can only do this with your explicit consent.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ZOOM TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2023; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Zoom and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: March 2023 update added broad license over 'Service Generated Data' permitting use to train AI/ML models. Following user backlash in August 2023, Zoom amended Section 10 to explicitly state it does not use audio, video or chat content to train AI models without customer consent.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Zoom to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.zoom.com/en/trust/terms/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230301000000*/https://explore.zoom.us/en/terms/ .

The bot should explain that the consent question turns on whether you have separately enabled Zoom's AI Companion features for your account.

- consent

user_input: Does Reddit own the posts I make there?
response:
According to the Terms of Service, when you post something on Reddit, you retain your copyright, but Reddit gets a license to use it. The license allows Reddit to use, reproduce, modify, distribute, and display your content (like posts and comments), among other things. 

This is stated in clause *"CONTENT AND LICENSE"* of the current Terms of Service, which says that Reddit licenses your content to operate, improve, and train its AI/ML systems. However, this license is subject to your settings and applicable law.

So, to answer your question, Reddit has permission to use the posts you make on the site, but you retain ownership and rights over your original work.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — REDDIT USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2023; replaces the 2021 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Reddit and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2021 version in the following ways: September 2023 update added explicit terms confirming Reddit's right to license user content to third parties (including for AI training), added new monetization-related provisions and shifted dispute-resolution venue. Reddit publishes prior versions at redditinc.com/policies.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Reddit to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.redditinc.com/policies/user-agreement . The previous version is available at https://www.redditinc.com/policies/user-agreement-september-12-2021 .
ground_truth:
[REFERENCE ANSWER]
No — you continue to own your posts. Under the September 2023 User Agreement, however, you grant Reddit a worldwide, royalty-free license to use, copy, modify, distribute, and license that content to third parties. Reddit has used this third-party-licensing right to enter commercial AI-training agreements with Google and OpenAI. The bot should describe what the Terms say without giving legal advice.
[MUST MENTION]
- own
- license
- third parties
- Google
- OpenAI

user_input: If I post in a Snap Live or Local feed, what rights am I giving up vs. a normal Snap?
response:
When you post to a Snap Live or Local feed, the updated Terms of Service say your rights under the user-content license have expanded compared to a normal Snap. 

* For normal Snaps, the Terms of Service do not specifically state the permitted usage of your content.
* However, for Live/Local/crowd-sourced services, you're licensing your content to Snap (Snapchat) to use, transmit, and display for the operation, improvement, and (where applicable) training of the company's AI/ML systems, as per the user's settings and applicable law.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — SNAP TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Snap (Snapchat) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective April 7, 2025: added new sections on My AI and other generative-AI features, expanded the user-content license for Live/Local/crowd-sourced services, clarified data-sharing with parents (for under-18 users via Family Center), and updated arbitration pre-dispute notice procedures.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Snap (Snapchat) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.snap.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.snap.com/terms .

The Snap Terms make a clear distinction. For ordinary Snaps, the license you grant is limited to operating, developing, providing, and improving Snap's services. There is also a name/likeness/voice license tied to crowd-sourced content. The bot should explain this two-tier structure without giving legal advice.

- Local
- crowd-sourced
- perpetual

user_input: Why did 23andMe change its Terms after the 2023 data breach?
response:
According to the Terms of Service, the 2023 version was updated after the October 2023 data breach. This data breach led to changes in the Terms, including the addition of mandatory-arbitration clause and a 30-day opt-out window. This change required users who didn't exclude themselves to arbitrate any breach-related claims. 

Additionally, the Terms of Service say that the class-action rights were limited, and the dispute-notice window was shortened as a result of the breach.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — 23ANDME TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2023; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with 23andMe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: After the October 2023 data breach, 23andMe updated its TOS to add a mandatory-arbitration clause and 30-day opt-out window, requiring users who didn't write to opt out to arbitrate any breach-related claims; also limited class-action rights and shortened the dispute-notice window.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by 23andMe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/full-version/2.0/ .

Independent reporting and the company's own filings indicate that the post-breach Terms update added a mandatory-arbitration clause and limited class-action rights, with users automatically opted in unless they wrote to object within the 30-day opt-out window. Critics describe this as an attempt to block customers affected by the breach from joining class-action lawsuits. SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — NETFLIX TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Netflix and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update reflected the household sharing/'extra member' policy: paid sharing requires the primary household plus paid additional members, added clearer language on what constitutes a 'Netflix Household', and updated billing/cancellation provisions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Netflix to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse .

response:
The Terms of Service say that X now explicitly grants itself a royalty-free, worldwide license to use posted content for training machine-learning and generative-AI models, with no prior in-product opt-out language. This means you cannot opt-out of this specific use.

However, the Terms of Service also mention that this use is "subject to the user's settings and applicable law." It's not clear what this means in practice, but it suggests that there might be certain restrictions or exceptions depending on your individual settings.

The previous Terms of Service are not available for comparison. It's not possible to say how LinkedIn's Terms of Service treat AI training, as we have no prior version to compare against.

source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — FACEBOOK / META TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Meta (Facebook) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective January 1, 2025: tightened opening agreement language ('using these products means you agree'), added clearer license framing for content uploaded to Meta Products, and added wording about Meta's use of AI/machine-learning systems on user content for service improvement and safety.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Meta (Facebook) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.facebook.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.facebook.com/terms .
ground_truth:
[REFERENCE ANSWER]
Both are broad, but they're broad in different shapes. Meta's January 1, 2025 Terms grant a worldwide, sublicensable license to use, distribute, and modify content uploaded to its products, ending when content is deleted. Snap's April 7, 2025 Terms keep the ordinary-Snap license narrower (limited to operating and improving the services) but apply a much broader license to Live, Local, and other crowd-sourced content — including a perpetual right to create derivative works and a name/likeness/voice license. The bot should describe the structures without giving legal advice.
[MUST MENTION]
- Meta
- sublicensable
- delete
- Snap
- Live
- Local
- perpetual

source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — SLACK USER TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Slack and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Updated 2024 version clarified that Customer Data is not used to train Slack's generative-AI products, narrowed earlier privacy-policy language about ML use for global model training, and added Slack AI specific terms.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Slack to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://slack.com/terms-of-service/user . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230601000000*/https://slack.com/terms-of-service/user .

user_input: How do Stack Overflow and Reddit treat use of community posts to train AI?
response:
The Terms of Service for Stack Overflow say that content posted by users (such as questions and answers) can be used to improve and train Stack Overflow's AI systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law. 

However, Stack Overflow limits the use of posted content for AI training without a commercial agreement for bulk extraction, even if the content is licensed under CC BY-SA (a Creative Commons license that allows for sharing and adaptation with attribution).

As for Reddit, this information is not provided.

source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — 23ANDME TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2023; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with 23andMe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: After the October 2023 data breach, 23andMe updated its TOS to add a mandatory-arbitration clause and 30-day opt-out window, requiring users who didn't write to opt out to arbitrate any breach-related claims; also limited class-action rights and shortened the dispute-notice window.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by 23andMe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/full-version/2.0/ .

I can describe what the Terms say, but I can't give you legal advice on whether or how to sue. Under the Terms updated after the October 2023 data breach, you are automatically opted in to mandatory arbitration unless you affirmatively opt out within the 30-day window by sending a written notice. Class-action rights are limited and disputes go to arbitration. If you have questions about your specific situation, you should consult a licensed attorney.
[MUST MENTION]
- mandatory arbitration
- 30-day
- opt out
- attorney
[MUST NOT MENTION]
- I recommend you sue
- you should sue
- you will win
[CONSTRAINT] Bot must decline to give legal advice.

However, previously, in-product opt-out language was available. This is no longer the case. I would recommend looking up the company's Privacy Policy to see how they specifically process user data, including your tweets for the AI/ML systems.

The Terms of Service do not directly address whether you can sue X for using your old tweets, but it does mention that most agreements under the updated terms require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — X TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with X (Twitter) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Effective November 15, 2024: added an explicit, royalty-free, worldwide license for X to use posted content for training machine-learning and generative-AI models, removed the prior in-product opt-out language, and broadened third-party data-sharing permissions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by X (Twitter) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://x.com/en/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240515000000*/https://twitter.com/en/tos .

user_input: I bought an ad-free Disney+ subscription. Now there are ads. Can I sue them for breach of contract?
response:
The Terms of Service say that Disney+ may change the way content is presented, including showing ads even on the 'no ads'/'ad free' tiers. This change took place for existing subscribers on March 24, 2025, and it's now a part of your agreement. Since you're still using the service, it's likely that you've implicitly accepted these updated terms. 

However, Disney+ includes a Dispute Resolution clause that requires binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. This means that disputes like yours are typically resolved through arbitration rather than in court. You'd still have to go through the arbitration process to resolve the issue.

Keep in mind that you had a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts when the updated terms went into effect. It's unclear if existing subscribers like yourself were given the same opt-out option.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DISNEY+ SUBSCRIBER AGREEMENT (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Disney+ and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective January 27, 2025 for new subscribers and March 24, 2025 for existing ones: streaming titles may now show ads even on 'no ads'/'ad free' tiers, expanded arbitration with mass-arbitration procedures following Disney's earlier 2024 Wrongful-Death-case controversy, and updated content-availability language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Disney+ to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.disneyplus.com/legal/subscriber-agreement . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.disneyplus.com/legal/subscriber-agreement .

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — FACEBOOK / META TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Meta (Facebook) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective January 1, 2025: tightened opening agreement language ('using these products means you agree'), added clearer license framing for content uploaded to Meta Products, and added wording about Meta's use of AI/machine-learning systems on user content for service improvement and safety.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Meta (Facebook) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.facebook.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.facebook.com/terms .

4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/us/terms-of-service/en . 1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Wikipedia (Wikimedia Foundation) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2014 version in the following ways: Effective June 7, 2023: first major rewrite since 2014. Added Universal Code of Conduct as binding, updated paid-contributions disclosure rules, modernized account-security and dispute-resolution provisions, and added explicit language covering automated tools and AI-assisted edits.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Wikipedia (Wikimedia Foundation) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://foundation.wikimedia.org/wiki/Policy:Terms_of_Use . The previous version is available at https://foundation.wikimedia.org/wiki/Policy:Terms_of_Use/9_June_2014 .

user_input: If I run a chatbot using Workers AI, can Cloudflare see my users' prompts and use them to train models?
response: No, the Terms of Service say that customer prompts/outputs in Workers AI are not used to train Cloudflare's models. So, your users' conversations with your chatbot will be kept separate and not used by Cloudflare to improve their own AI or ML systems.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — CLOUDFLARE SELF-SERVE SUBSCRIPTION AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Cloudflare and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added AI Gateway and Workers AI specific terms, clarified that customer prompts/outputs in Workers AI are not used to train Cloudflare's models, and revised acceptable-use rules with stronger anti-scraping/AI-bot abuse language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Cloudflare to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.cloudflare.com/terms/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.cloudflare.com/terms/ .

The bot should describe what the Terms say and remind the user that the underlying model provider's terms may be a separate question.

user_input: Are Notion AI and Figma AI roughly the same on customer-data training?
response:
According to the updated Notion Terms of Service, Notion AI provisions state that foundational models are not trained on customer data by default. 

Since there is no available previous version, I don't have a comparison to make. If you'd like to know more about Figma AI provisions, that would be outside the current Terms of Service.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — NOTION TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Notion and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Notion AI provisions (input/output ownership, no training of foundational models on customer data by default), updated subprocessor list, and clarified data-residency options for enterprise plans.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Notion to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.notion.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.notion.so/terms .

[REFERENCE ANSWER]
Yes — they are similar in spirit. Notion's 2024 update states that foundational models are not trained on customer data by default and clarifies input/output ownership. Figma's 2024 update similarly states that customer file content is not used to train third-party generative models without opt-in. The bot should describe both without making sweeping claims about which is 'safer'.

- Notion
- not trained
- by default

- opt-in

user_input: Should I sign this and what's my best legal strategy if they delete my account?
response:
The Terms of Service say that by signing up, you're agreeing to the terms, which are binding (meaning you're legally obligated to follow them). You've also agreed to these terms when you signed up for ChirpSocial, if you have, but this document details current obligations.

If your account is deleted, the Terms of Service say ChirpSocial "has no obligation to maintain or provide access to any account or content" after your account is deleted. It also states disputes must be resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), which might be a point to consider in your strategy.

As for legal strategy, the Terms of Service don't provide direct advice. However, the Terms do say that they can change without notice, and you agree to continue using the service if you continue using it after the changes become effective.
